problem_text:
A logistics firm must devise a procurement and stock management scheme for a critical component across a 15-week operational timeline.  
Initial stock at the outset of the planning window is 90 units.  
In each week \( t = 1, \dots, 15 \), the vendor permits the firm to submit a procurement request whose size must fall between 11 and 72 units.  
Nevertheless, every order submitted requires a lead time of 2 weeks before it becomes available to meet requirements or augment stock levels.  
Weekly requirements for the component are enumerated below:  

* Week 1: requirement 24 units  
* Week 2: requirement 36 units  
* Week 3: requirement 34 units  
* Week 4: requirement 40 units  
* Week 5: requirement 10 units  
* Week 6: requirement 37 units  
* Week 7: requirement 23 units  
* Week 8: requirement 34 units  
* Week 9: requirement 58 units  
* Week 10: requirement 12 units  
* Week 11: requirement 49 units  
* Week 12: requirement 27 units  
* Week 13: requirement 11 units  
* Week 14: requirement 47 units  
* Week 15: requirement 32 units  

Stockouts are permissible, but any unsatisfied requirement is considered lost and will not be carried forward.  
Throughout the planning interval, component quantities may be treated as continuous, and the aggregate quantity of physical stock on hand at any moment must remain within the storage limit of 90 units.  
Cumulative expenditure over the planning horizon comprises three elements: the procurement expense, amounting to 6 per unit acquired; the storage expense, amounting to 2 per unit retained from one week to the next; and the stockout penalty, amounting to 8 per unit of unfulfilled requirement.  
The objective is to identify the optimal acquisition quantity each week and to monitor the consequent stock and deficit levels so as to minimize total expenditure.
